content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

Section 19 already sits at or above our preferred WARRANTY position:

- **Services standard** (§19.1): professional and workmanlike, qualified personnel, industry standards, plus an untimed general conformity warranty for Services and Deliverables.
- **Duration** (§19.2): 90 days per Deliverable — and since "Deliverable" (§1.4) is bespoke work product rather than licensed software, 90 days is exactly our preferred services-side period. The software/hosted element is warranted to conform **throughout the subscription term**, which beats our 12-month preferred software period.
- **Remedy** (§19.4): prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination and refund of Fees, and expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. Acceptance-stage relief also exists at §6.2.
- **Other warranties** (§19.3): compliance with Applicable Law, no malicious code, no functionality diminution, open-source protection.
- **Disclaimer does not swallow the warranty** (§19.5): mutual implied-warranty disclaimer only, with an express carve-out preserving express warranties, service levels, indemnities and data-protection duties.

Only soft spot noted for the record: the malicious-code warranty is limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor." That qualifier is market-standard and, against a term-long hosted conformity warranty and non-exclusive remedies, does not justify a redline here.

reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and, consistent with that status, no redline or counterparty comment was proposed — appropriate here since nothing needs to change to reach the preferred position ('No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer').

The cited text supports compliance: Section 7.1 limits Customer's payment obligation to Order Form Fees and expressly bars unidentified minimum-use or similar charges; the rationale further cites Section 27.3 ('without penalty') and Section 24.4 (no acceleration on change of control). No 'as liquidated damages', penalty, or early-termination-fee mechanic is present.

The Section 2.1 take-or-pay commitment is correctly characterized as a minimum-commitment exposure routed to the MINCOMMIT rule rather than a stipulated-damages/penalty mechanic, so treating LD as met by silence is a defensible, non-duplicative allocation.

Caveat for downstream review: because 2.1 states the commitment applies 'without reduction or termination rights', the residual commitment could function like a minimum fee on termination — the MINCOMMIT finding should ensure that survival-on-termination effect is actually addressed (e.g., commitment reduced/released on termination for cause, or any residual capped at 3 months' fees), since the LD rule will not pick it up.

input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment on Customer expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — the playbook walk-away position. It also conflicts with Section 7.1 (no unstated minimum-use charge) and Section 12.3 (Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment). We replaced it with the preferred position: no minimum commitment, non-binding forecasts, and Fees payable only for Services ordered or used; fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up not penalty) offered in the comment.

ops.newText: 2.1 Customer has no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment under this Agreement. Any volume or spend figures the Parties exchange are non-binding forecasts, and Customer is obligated to pay only the Fees for Services actually ordered under an Order Form or actually used.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination right, so we have replaced Section 2.1 with a non-binding forecast: we pay for Services we order or use. This also removes the conflict with Sections 7.1 and 12.3, which already state that no minimum-use charge or minimum-volume commitment applies. If a commitment is commercially essential, we could consider one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: Section 19 meets or exceeds our preferred position. §19.1 gives a professional/workmanlike and qualified-personnel warranty plus a general conformity warranty for Services and Deliverables with no time limit; §19.2 gives 90 days for each Deliverable (which under §1.4 is custom work product, i.e., the services-side item for which 90 days is our preferred period) and, for the software/hosted element, conformity throughout the entire subscription term, which is longer than our 12-month preferred software period. §19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law, a no-malicious-code warranty, and no-functionality-diminution and open-source protections. §19.4 supplies the full preferred remedy stack — prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, and termination with refund of Fees if not cured within a reasonable period — and expressly preserves other remedies for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. §19.5 confirms the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties, service levels, indemnities or data-protection duties. content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

Section 19 already sits at or above our preferred WARRANTY position:

- **Services standard** (§19.1): professional and workmanlike, qualified personnel, industry standards, plus an untimed general conformity warranty for Services and Deliverables.
- **Duration** (§19.2): 90 days per Deliverable — and since "Deliverable" (§1.4) is bespoke work product rather than licensed software, 90 days is exactly our preferred services-side period. The software/hosted element is warranted to conform **throughout the subscription term**, which beats our 12-month preferred software period.
- **Remedy** (§19.4): prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination and refund of Fees, and expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. Acceptance-stage relief also exists at §6.2.
- **Other warranties** (§19.3): compliance with Applicable Law, no malicious code, no functionality diminution, open-source protection.
- **Disclaimer does not swallow the warranty** (§19.5): mutual implied-warranty disclaimer only, with an express carve-out preserving express warranties, service levels, indemnities and data-protection duties.

Only soft spot noted for the record: the malicious-code warranty is limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor." That qualifier is market-standard and, against a term-long hosted conformity warranty and non-exclusive remedies, does not justify a redline here.

**Finding: Deviation (Section 2.1)**

Section 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment on us for three years, expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — squarely the playbook walk-away position. It also contradicts Section 7.1 (Vendor may not impose an unstated minimum-use charge) and Section 12.3 (Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment).

Redline validated (ok:true) and submitted: Section 2.1 is replaced so that there is no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment, volume figures are non-binding forecasts, and Fees are payable only for Services ordered or used. The comment offers the fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up rather than penalty) if a commitment is commercially essential.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment on Customer expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — the playbook walk-away position. It also conflicts with Section 7.1 (no unstated minimum-use charge) and Section 12.3 (Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment). We replaced it with the preferred position: no minimum commitment, non-binding forecasts, and Fees payable only for Services ordered or used; fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up not penalty) offered in the comment.

Original paragraphs:
p0012: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Juniper Ridge Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Cobalt Cloud Services LLC, a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Services: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

Rendered redline:
p0012: 2.1 Customer has no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment under this Agreement. Any volume or spend figures the Parties exchange are non-binding forecasts, and Customer is obligated to pay only the Fees for Services actually ordered under an Order Form or actually used.

Comment:
[Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination right, so we have replaced Section 2.1 with a non-binding forecast: we pay for Services we order or use. This also removes the conflict with Sections 7.1 and 12.3, which already state that no minimum-use charge or minimum-volume commitment applies. If a commitment is commercially essential, we could consider one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: 10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
input.rationale: Section 10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination) addresses only access wind-down (10.1) and Deliverable delivery plus refunds (10.2). There is no transition-assistance period, no obligation to return or export Customer Data in a machine-readable format, and no deletion or deletion-certification obligation; searches for "transition assistance", "export" and "delete" return nothing relevant, and Section 16.5 expressly carves Customer Data out to "Sections 11 and 15" while Section 11 does not exist in the document. Section 15 covers processing limits only. In a hosted services agreement this absence is a deviation, so we insert a new Section 10.3 with six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return of Customer Data within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter.

input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
input.rationale: Substantively the Section 19 warranty package meets or exceeds our preferred position: §19.1 gives the professional/workmanlike and qualified-personnel standard plus an untimed conformity warranty; §19.2 gives 90 days for each Deliverable (custom work product under §1.4, matching our preferred services-side period) and term-long conformity for Hosted Services, which exceeds the 12-month software preference; §19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law and a no-malicious-code warranty; §19.4 supplies re-performance/repair/replacement plus termination and refund of Fees, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims; and §19.5 prevents the disclaimer from swallowing the express warranties. The single defect is drafting: the warranty period is spelled out in words only ("For ninety days"), with no numeral, which leaves the key parameter less certain than the rest of the Agreement's convention and risks argument over the measured period. The minimal redline inserts "(90)" so the period reads "ninety (90) days"; no substantive term is changed, and the malicious-code qualifier ("intentionally introduced by Vendor") remains an acceptable market-standard concession given the non-exclusive remedy stack.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
input.rationale: Section 19 meets or exceeds our preferred position. §19.1 gives a professional/workmanlike and qualified-personnel warranty plus a general conformity warranty for Services and Deliverables with no time limit; §19.2 gives 90 days for each Deliverable (which under §1.4 is custom work product, i.e., the services-side item for which 90 days is our preferred period) and, for the software/hosted element, conformity throughout the entire subscription term, which is longer than our 12-month preferred software period. §19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law, a no-malicious-code warranty, and no-functionality-diminution and open-source protections. §19.4 supplies the full preferred remedy stack — prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, and termination with refund of Fees if not cured within a reasonable period — and expressly preserves other remedies for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. §19.5 confirms the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties, service levels, indemnities or data-protection duties. The only softening is that the malicious-code warranty in §19.3 is limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor"; this is market-standard and, given the term-long hosted conformity warranty and non-exclusive remedies, is not worth a redline.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

Section 19 already sits at or above our preferred WARRANTY position:

- **Services standard** (§19.1): professional and workmanlike, qualified personnel, industry standards, plus an untimed general conformity warranty for Services and Deliverables.
- **Duration** (§19.2): 90 days per Deliverable — and since "Deliverable" (§1.4) is bespoke work product rather than licensed software, 90 days is exactly our preferred services-side period. The software/hosted element is warranted to conform **throughout the subscription term**, which beats our 12-month preferred software period.
- **Remedy** (§19.4): prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination and refund of Fees, and expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. Acceptance-stage relief also exists at §6.2.
- **Other warranties** (§19.3): compliance with Applicable Law, no malicious code, no functionality diminution, open-source protection.
- **Disclaimer does not swallow the warranty** (§19.5): mutual implied-warranty disclaimer only, with an express carve-out preserving express warranties, service levels, indemnities and data-protection duties.

Only soft spot noted for the record: the malicious-code warranty is limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor." That qualifier is market-standard and, against a term-long hosted conformity warranty and non-exclusive remedies, does not justify a redline here.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
Section 10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination) addresses only access wind-down (10.1) and Deliverable delivery plus refunds (10.2). There is no transition-assistance period, no obligation to return or export Customer Data in a machine-readable format, and no deletion or deletion-certification obligation; searches for "transition assistance", "export" and "delete" return nothing relevant, and Section 16.5 expressly carves Customer Data out to "Sections 11 and 15" while Section 11 does not exist in the document. Section 15 covers processing limits only. In a hosted services agreement this absence is a deviation, so we insert a new Section 10.3 with six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return of Customer Data within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter.

Original paragraphs:
p0042: 10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Juniper Ridge Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Cobalt Cloud Services LLC, a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Juniper Ridge Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Cobalt Cloud Services LLC, a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Deliverable: 1.4 “Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.
Fees: 1.5 “Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.
Services: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

Rendered redline:
p0042: 10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
10.3 Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty days of Customer's request, return or make available for download all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems, subject to routine backups and legal retention requirements, and certify such deletion in writing.

Comment:
[Playbook] Section 10 winds down access and Deliverables but says nothing about exit support or getting our data back, so we have added a transition-assistance and data-return provision: up to six months' assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is an issue we can accept ninety days of assistance, provided the thirty-day export and deletion certification remain.

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 19 meets or exceeds the preferred WARRANTY position, so no redline is warranted. §19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike standard performed by qualified personnel to industry standards, plus an untimed warranty that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to documentation and specifications. §19.2 gives 90 days after the later of delivery or acceptance for each Deliverable — and because "Deliverable" under §1.4 is bespoke work product (reports, configurations, integrations, training material) rather than licensed software, 90 days matches our preferred services-side period; the software/hosted element is warranted to conform throughout the whole subscription term, exceeding our 12-month preferred software period. §19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law, a no-malicious-code warranty, and no-functionality-diminution and open-source protections. §19.4 delivers the full preferred remedy stack: prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination of the affected item and refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure within a reasonable period, and expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims; §6.2 adds acceptance-stage correction and refund rights. §19.5 confirms the disclaimer is mutual, limited to implied warranties, and does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality or data-protection duty, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty. The only softening is that the malicious-code warranty is limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor," which is market-standard and does not undercut the position given the non-exclusive remedies; it is not worth reopening a favourable package. The spelled-out "ninety days" phrasing is legally unambiguous and is a drafting-convention point only, not a substantive shortfall.

Original paragraphs:
p0071: 19.1 Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.
p0072: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
p0073: 19.3 Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.
p0074: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.
p0075: 19.5 Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Juniper Ridge Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Cobalt Cloud Services LLC, a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Juniper Ridge Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Cobalt Cloud Services LLC, a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Applicable Law: 1.2 “Applicable Law” means every statute, regulation, binding regulatory requirement, court order, and governmental rule applicable to a Party's performance under this Agreement, including laws concerning privacy, information security, export controls, employment, anti-bribery, and accessibility. Applicable Law does not include a private standard unless an Order Form expressly adopts it.
Deliverable: 1.4 “Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.
Fees: 1.5 “Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Order Form: 1.6 “Order Form” means a written ordering document signed by authorized representatives of both Parties that references this Agreement and describes the Services, Deliverables, subscription quantities, service levels, Fees, and term purchased by Customer. A purchase order is an administrative convenience only and does not amend an Order Form or this Agreement.
Services: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

p0074: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-4b4a32cd","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 19.5 Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.","rationale":"The Agreement contains no indemnification provision. The outline jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) straight to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), so Section 20 is absent entirely: there is no Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused data compromise, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and no indemnification procedure. Other clauses assume the section exists — Section 9.3 conditions Customer's termination right on Vendor's inability to \"provide the remedies required by Section 20.5\", Section 19.4 preserves remedies for \"indemnified claims\", Section 21.3 makes \"its indemnification obligations\" an Excluded Claim, and Section 30.5 refers to an \"indemnified party\" and \"vested indemnity rights\" — leaving dangling cross-references. This is a critical gap approaching the walk-away position (no Vendor IP indemnity at all). We therefore insert a new Section 20 after Section 19.5 implementing the preferred position: Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates for IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access to Customer Data, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law; standard notice/control/cooperation procedure; customary IP exclusions; and Section 20.5 procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, which also repairs the Section 9.3 cross-reference. No liability super-cap is needed because Section 21.3 already carves indemnification obligations out of the cap.","proposal":"Insert new Section 20 (Indemnification): Vendor defence/indemnity for IP, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; narrow Customer indemnity; standard procedure; and Section 20.5 infringement remedies referenced by Section 9.3.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-4c5e622c","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.","rationale":"§ 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of Deliverables that, per the § 1.4 definition, are work product \"created specifically for Customer\" (and expressly exclude Vendor Technology and Vendor know-how), while leaving us only a revocable, non-transferable licence limited to the Order Form term. That inverts the playbook position that we own what we pay for, and the revocable term licence means we lose access to our own bespoke reports, configurations and integrations at expiry. §§ 14.1 and 15.1 correctly leave Customer Data and Customer IP with us, § 14.3 properly preserves Vendor Technology with the perpetual § 13.2 licence-back, and § 14.4 disclaims joint ownership — so the only defect is the ownership direction in § 14.2. Redline vests Deliverable ownership in Customer with a present assignment, expressly preserving Vendor's retained Vendor Technology rights under § 14.3; fallback (perpetual, irrevocable § 13.2-style licence over the whole Deliverable) is offered in the comment.","proposal":"Reverse § 14.2 so Customer owns paid-for Deliverables, with Vendor assignment and Vendor Technology carve-out preserved.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-7df8de07","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","rationale":"Section 21.1 imposes a mutual cap at the greater of Fees paid or payable by Customer in the 12 months preceding the event and USD 1,000,000, exactly the preferred basis. Section 21.2 excludes indirect/consequential damages mutually and confirms data restoration, replacement services, breach notification and incident response costs are direct damages. Section 21.3 defines \"Excluded Claims\" to cover confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP; because both 21.1 and 21.2 open \"Except for Excluded Claims,\" those carve-outs sit outside the cap and are uncapped rather than merely excluded. Section 21.3 also confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not \"damages\" and is not limited. \"Fees\" (§1.5) covers recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so with the §2.1 commitment of USD 2,000,000 per year the 12-month fee basis is meaningful, not illusory. Section 21.4 preserves unlimited liability where it cannot lawfully be limited and makes each cap independent of failure of an exclusive remedy; §18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities, and no competing cap or one-sided \"aggregate liability\" language appears in the warranty, indemnity or insurance provisions. No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-f67decf2","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","rationale":"Section 24 meets our preferred position. § 24.1 gives us a consent-free right to assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor (notice only); § 24.2 binds Vendor to our prior written consent (reasonableness standard) for assignment, delegation of material performance or transfer by change of control, and bars assignment to a direct competitor; § 24.3's residual consent requirement is expressly limited to \"other assignments\" and so does not swallow the § 24.1 carve-out; and § 24.4 confirms our change of control gives Vendor no right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees or reduce service. § 13.3 tracks Section 24 by allowing licence transfer to an Affiliate or permitted successor. No change-of-control or assignment trigger for Vendor termination appears elsewhere (§ 9.2 is insolvency-only). No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-f8a3982b","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.","rationale":"Section 7.2 binds Customer, not Vendor: before engaging any other provider we must surrender the terms of a competing offer and give Vendor the chance to match. That is a right of first refusal amounting to de facto exclusivity (plus an MFC-style disclosure duty), which the playbook prohibits, and it compounds the Section 2.1 take-or-pay minimum by making it impractical to source elsewhere. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment. Preferred position is deletion; a narrow category-limited 12-month first-look right with automatic termination on service-level or delivery failure is the fallback. The non-exclusive licence grants and Vendor-side exclusivity provisions elsewhere are unobjectionable.","proposal":"Delete Section 7.2 disclose-and-match obligation that creates de facto exclusivity on Customer.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-1485ba79","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.","rationale":"Searches for \"liquidated\", \"penalty\", \"termination fee\", \"convenience\", \"accelerat\", and \"minimum\" return no provision requiring Customer to pay liquidated damages, a penalty, an early-termination fee, or accelerated/minimum fees on termination. Section 7.1 limits Customer's payment obligation to Order Form Fees and bars unidentified minimum-use or similar charges; Section 27.3 expressly lets Customer terminate \"without penalty\"; Section 24.4 bars Vendor from accelerating Fees on a Customer change of control. The only Customer-payable exposures are the Section 2.1 take-or-pay volume commitment (a minimum-commitment issue addressed under the MINCOMMIT rule, not a liquidated-damages or penalty mechanic) and the Section 22.2 audit-shortfall cost shift (actual amounts owed, not a stipulated penalty). Nothing in the document imposes liquidated damages on Customer, so the preferred position is met by silence and no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-a6ceb0b7","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.","rationale":"Sections 13.1–13.3 already meet the preferred position for the Services and paid-up software: they name Affiliates and contractors, grant a perpetual, irrevocable paid-up licence, allow transfer to an Affiliate or successor, and permit revocation only for material uncured breach after notice and cure. Section 14.2 is inconsistent and falls to the walk-away position for Deliverables: the licence is expressly revocable, non-transferable, limited to the Order Form term, and silent on Affiliates and contractors, even though Deliverables are work product created specifically for and paid for by Customer. The redline conforms § 14.2 to the § 13.2/13.3 bargain (perpetual, irrevocable, Affiliates and contractors covered, transferable to an Affiliate or successor, revocation only per § 13.3), which is the smallest edit reaching the preferred position while leaving Vendor's ownership of Deliverables intact.","proposal":"Conform the Deliverable licence in § 14.2 to the perpetual, irrevocable, transferable grant in §§ 13.2–13.3 and extend it to Affiliates and contractors.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-aa0c1dbb","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.","rationale":"§ 7.2 is a reverse MFN: the obligation runs against Customer (Juniper Ridge), requiring us to surface any more favourable third-party commercial offer and match it for Vendor before engaging another provider. That is an open-ended obligation to extend Vendor better terms obtained from third parties, which the playbook treats as unacceptable (walk-away territory) and is inconsistent with § 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. No Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document, so nothing beneficial to us is lost by deletion. Preferred remedy: delete § 7.2 entirely; fallback would be an MFN limited to one defined product, 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.","proposal":"Delete reverse MFN obligation on Customer in § 7.2.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-00a4a55e","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.","rationale":"§ 12.4 imposes a post-term non-compete on Customer for 24 months, worldwide (\"in any territory\"), covering any product or service that \"competes with Vendor\" — undefined scope and beyond the 12-month walk-away limit. It binds our party (not the Vendor) and restricts our ability to develop, buy, or sell products, which the playbook rejects outright. It also contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no non-compete commitment. Preferred remedy is deletion; a named-product, term-only, 12-month restriction with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs is the fallback if Vendor presses.","proposal":"Delete the 24-month worldwide non-compete binding Customer in § 12.4.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-b0a0546d","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 9 TERMINATION","rationale":"The Agreement runs for three years (Section 8.1) and Section 9 provides only cause-based termination rights (material breach, insolvency, security/service-level/legal/IP failures); no Customer termination for convenience exists, and Section 2.1 expressly negates any reduction or termination right against a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay commitment. Under T4C, absence of a Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation. Vendor has no convenience right today, so we preserve that by making it explicit. We insert a new Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no penalty, and overriding Section 2.1, matching the preferred position.","proposal":"Insert Section 9.4 granting Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund and no Vendor convenience right.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-21890795","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.","rationale":"Section 22 meets every element of the preferred position: audits are limited to once per twelve-month period (22.1), require thirty days' prior written notice during normal business hours (22.1), are conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (22.1), are at Vendor's cost unless the audit establishes underpayment exceeding five percent (22.2), and expressly bar Vendor and its auditor from accessing Customer systems directly or unrelated Customer Data, privileged material, or other suppliers' confidential information (22.2). Section 22.3 adds Customer-favourable protections (findings are Customer Confidential Information, use limited to enforcement, copy of final report, payment resolves the issue). Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) contains only a heading with no substantive paragraphs, so it creates no broader audit or inspection path against Customer, and no other clause in the Agreement grants Vendor inspection, verification, or monitoring rights over Customer. No redline is required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-4a18e833","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.","rationale":"Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and is close to the walk-away position of a foreign venue. It also directly conflicts with Section 28.2, which grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County. We replaced only the jurisdiction words in 28.1 with New York law and deleted the redundant Singapore venue grant, so that Section 28.2's New York County forum controls; the Section 28.3 executive escalation process is acceptable and no arbitration clause exists in the document.","proposal":"Replace Singapore governing law and venue with New York law, leaving New York County courts as the exclusive forum.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-953097f3","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","rationale":"Section 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment on Customer expressly \"without reduction or termination rights\" — the playbook walk-away position. It also conflicts with Section 7.1 (no unstated minimum-use charge) and Section 12.3 (Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment). {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** Legal (In-House Counsel)
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — issues, positions and next steps

---

## Executive Summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The commercial architecture is workable in several respects, but the risk allocation is materially one-sided against us in four critical or high-risk areas, three of which sit at or near our walk-away thresholds.

The single most serious gap is the **complete absence of an indemnification section**. The outline runs from Section 19 (Warranties) directly to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), so there is no Vendor defence or indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused data compromise, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. Several surviving clauses assume that section exists — §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all cross-reference indemnity concepts — leaving dangling references that must be repaired.

We also face an **inverted intellectual property position**: § 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of bespoke Deliverables in the Vendor and leaves us a revocable, non-transferable licence expiring with the Order Form term, meaning we lose access to work product we paid for. Separately, the Agreement loads a cluster of **one-way restrictive covenants onto us** — a reverse most-favoured-nation disclose-and-match obligation (§ 7.2), a 24-month worldwide non-compete and a 24-month no-hire (§ 12.4) — each of which contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor expressly acknowledges we made no such commitments. That internal inconsistency strengthens our deletion arguments considerably. Finally, § 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights," with no offsetting termination for convenience anywhere in Section 9.

On the positive side, the limitation of liability package (Section 21), assignment and change-of-control provisions (Section 24), audit rights (Section 22), renewal mechanics (Section 8), insurance (Section 18) and the liquidated-damages position all meet or exceed our preferred positions and require no redline. Governing law is a straightforward fix: § 28.1 selects Singapore but directly conflicts with § 28.2, which already grants exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts.

One finding — the warranty analysis under Section 19 — did not clear verification and is flagged for review before we rely on it.

---

Insert new Section 20 with Vendor defence/indemnity for IP, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; narrow Customer indemnity; standard procedure; and § 20.5 remedies. No super-cap needed as § 21.3 already carves indemnification out of the cap. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor owns bespoke Deliverables; we get only a revocable, term-limited licence. Reverse so Customer owns paid-for Deliverables via present assignment, preserving Vendor Technology under § 14.3. Fallback: perpetual, irrevocable § 13.2-style licence over the whole Deliverable. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 | Mutual cap at greater of trailing 12-month Fees or USD 1,000,000; Excluded Claims (§ 21.3) sit outside the cap and are uncapped. No redline. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 | Consent-free Customer assignment to Affiliate or M&A successor; Vendor bound by consent and competitor bar. No redline. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Disclose-and-match obligation is a right of first refusal creating de facto exclusivity; compounds § 2.1 take-or-pay and contradicts § 12.3. Delete. Fallback: category-limited 12-month first-look, terminating on service-level or delivery failure. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 7.1 | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee; § 27.3 permits termination "without penalty." No redline. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 14.2 | Deliverable licence is revocable, non-transferable, term-limited and silent on Affiliates/contractors — inconsistent with §§ 13.1–13.3. Conform § 14.2 to the perpetual, irrevocable, transferable § 13.2/13.3 grant. |

| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | 24-month, worldwide, undefined-scope post-term non-compete binding us; exceeds 12-month walk-away limit and contradicts § 12.3. Delete. Fallback: named product, term-only plus 12 months, with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 9 (Termination) | Three-year term (§ 8.1) with cause-based termination only, against a § 2.1 take-or-pay with no reduction rights. Insert § 9.4: Customer convenience right on 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund, no penalty, overriding § 2.1, with no reciprocal Vendor right. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, independent auditor, cost-shift only above 5% underpayment, no direct system access. No redline. |

Insert § 10.3: six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Needs review (verification failed)** | § 19.1 | Analysis concludes Section 19 meets or exceeds our preferred position and requires no redline, but this finding did not pass verification. To be re-confirmed before we rely on it. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 | CGL USD 1M/2M, workers' comp, employer's liability USD 1M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M for term plus one year; § 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit liability. No redline. |

---

## Walk-Away Items

The following provisions sit at or approaching our stated walk-away positions. We should not sign without resolution.

1. **No Vendor IP indemnity (§ 20 absent).** The total absence of any Vendor defence or indemnity — including for third-party IP infringement — approaches the walk-away position. The dangling cross-references in §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 confirm the section was intended to exist.
2. **Deliverable licence terms (§ 14.2).** The revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence, silent on Affiliates and contractors, falls to the walk-away position on licence scope and is internally inconsistent with the perpetual, irrevocable grant we already have in §§ 13.2–13.3.
3. **Take-or-pay minimum commitment (§ 2.1).** A three-year USD 2,000,000-per-year commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights" is the walk-away formulation, and it conflicts with both § 7.1 and § 12.3.
4. **Reverse MFN (§ 7.2).** An open-ended obligation to extend Vendor better terms obtained from third parties is unacceptable and is contradicted by § 12.3.
5. **Non-compete (§ 12.4).** A 24-month, worldwide, undefined-scope restriction exceeds the 12-month limit and binds the wrong party.
6. **No-hire (§ 12.4).** A one-way 24-month no-hire with no general-advertising or unsolicited-applicant carve-out sits at the walk-away edge.
7. **Foreign governing law and venue (§ 28.1).** Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction is close to the walk-away position, and is in any event irreconcilable with § 28.2.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline** implementing the proposals above: insert Section 20 (Indemnification) with § 20.5 infringement remedies to repair the § 9.3 cross-reference; reverse ownership and conform the licence in § 14.2; insert § 9.4 (termination for convenience) and § 10.3 (transition assistance, data return, certified deletion); replace § 2.1; delete § 7.2 and § 12.4; and substitute New York law in § 28.1.
2. **Lead the covenant discussion with § 12.3.** Vendor's own acknowledgement that we made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment directly contradicts §§ 2.1, 7.2 and 12.4. We should present these as drafting conflicts to be resolved in our favour rather than as negotiated concessions.
3. **Resolve the § 20 numbering gap with Vendor.** Confirm whether the indemnity section was omitted in error and request their standard language as a starting point, while tabling our own draft.
4. **Re-verify the WARRANTY finding (§ 19).** That finding failed verification; we will re-review Section 19 before confirming that no redline is required.
5. **Confirm the § 16.5 cross-reference.** Section 16.5 carves Customer Data out to "Sections 11 and 15," but Section 11 does not appear in the document. We will raise this with Vendor alongside the § 10.3 insertion.
6. **Hold the compliant provisions.** Sections 8, 18, 21, 22 and 24 meet or exceed our positions; we should resist any reopening of these as trade currency.
7. **Brief the business** on the § 2.1 and § 7.2 positions, since removing the take-or-pay and the disclose-and-match right materially changes the commercial model Vendor has proposed."}
